title: Skip Counting in 5s, 7s, 60s, 100s and 1,000s
seo_title: Skip Counting – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count in groups of 5s, 7s and 60s, and in 100s and 1,000s up to 10,000; solve quantitative reasoning problems with number patterns. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on skip counting: count on and back in 5s, 7s, 60s, 100s and 1,000s, find missing numbers and solve counting problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Add the same step each time
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Skip counting means adding the same number (the step) each time: 7, 14, 21, 28, …
  • Find the step by subtracting two numbers next to each other.
  • Counting in 60s helps with time: 60 minutes = 1 hour.

Examples

Example

60, 120, 180, 240, …

The step is 60

Answer: 300

Example

3,000, 4,000, ___, 6,000

Count in 1,000s

Answer: 5,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the wrong stepCheck the difference between two numbers next to each other.
Adding when counting backCounting back means subtracting.
Losing a zero in big steps3,000 + 1,000 = 4,000, not 3,100.

faq.a: There are 7 days in a week, so counting in 7s helps with weeks and the 7 times table.
